By Charlotte Goldstone
13 October 2026
AI is everywhere in logistics right now, but what does it actually mean for freight forwarding?
In this episode of The Loadstar Podcast, host Charlotte Goldstone speaks to Erik Muttersbach, founder of Zauber and former Forto technology executive, about where AI and agentic AI really stand today, what is already happening in forwarding, and what could change over the next three to five years.
Erik shares what he is learning from real-world deployments with customers, tackles some of the biggest misconceptions around AI, and explains why adoption and change management may be just as important as the technology itself.
They also discuss the buy-versus-build question, the patterns Erik has seen across a decade of technology adoption in forwarding, and how companies can separate genuine AI capability from the hype. Looking ahead, what will AI actually change across the forwarding value chain – and which parts of the industry will prove hardest to transform?

LEGO Launches the Mother of All Mash-Ups, Ideas Challenge Needs Star Wars Mixed with Marvel
6 photos
Photo: LEGO
I’ve heard people mistaking the Star Wars universe for that of Star Trek, and I even know some who can’t tell the difference between a Marvel superhero and a DC one. Until this week, though, I've never heard of anyone mixing up the worlds of interstellar travel and adventure with that of suited people with powers.
Well, guess what? Danish toy maker LEGO announced what may very well be one of the wackiest Ideas challenges in ages: a mash-up between the worlds and characters of Star Wars and Marvel, which will forever be immortalized in plastic brick form.
The new LEGO Ideas challenge was officially announced this past weekend during the New York Comic Con, and, to be fair, did not pop into the heads of LEGO’s peeps out of the blue. As you know, there’s a new comic series coming out at the beginning of next year.
It’s called Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles, and it is the first-ever crossover between the two universes. At the same time, it’s also one of the ways the Star Wars franchise chose to celebrate its 50th anniversary next year.
So, what is this new LEGO Ideas challenge all about? Well, for one, there are three themes fan designers can choose from: vehicles, characters, and scenes. Once a theme is selected, the build can officially begin, and, when that’s over as well, the designs can be submitted to LEGO Ideas for review.
From there, the process is as straightforward as possible. People can vote on a submitted idea until certain thresholds are reached. LEGO doesn’t specifically say what that would be in this case, but, in general, a set must be voted for by at least 10,000 people to be considered for production.
There are, of course, some rules for the build process itself. The first is that any set created as part of the challenge must contain characters that are part of the Star Wars: A New Hope movie and any Marvel comics.
Then, the resulting set must be an original creation and combine elements that are part of each of the two worlds. That means sets that depict only one of the two will not be allowed in. Finally, the sets imagined for this challenge must contain a minimum of 400 pieces of plastic and a maximum of 3,000.
LEGO says voting for the Ideas submitted as part of this challenge will open on December 15, 2026, while the sets selected for the grand prize will be announced on an unspecified date next year.
Naturally, we’ll keep an eye on this and report back when strange designs like a Tony Stark-made Stormtrooper, Doctor Strange fighting alongside the Rebel Alliance, or perhaps Darth Vader chasing the Infinity Stones come to light.

The Port of Los Angeles handled 1,042,652 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in September, making it the busiest month in the port’s 118-year history. Cargo volume rose 18.1% from the previous year, beating the previous monthly record set in July 2025 by more than 20,000 containers .
What’s Related
September also capped the port’s busiest quarter, with approximately 3 million TEUs handled from July through September. The June-through-September stretch reached nearly 4 million TEUs, setting a separate four-month record.
Imports reached an all-time monthly high of 546,696 TEUs, up 19% from September 2025 and 26% above the port’s five-year average. Exports increased 10% to 125,571 TEUs, while empty containers rose 20.4% to a record 371,206 TEUs.
Through the first nine months of the year, the port handled 8,081,625 TEUs, up 3.38% from the same period in 2025. Executive Director Gene Seroka said those results put Los Angeles on a strong pace heading into the fourth quarter.
RELATED: Top 30 U.S. Ports Ranked By Container Imports
Holiday merchandise and inventory replenishments
On a media call, Seroka pointed to lower tariffs , continued consumer spending, and shipping disruptions as reasons for the increase. Major retailers and other importers are bringing in holiday merchandise while replenishing inventories.
“A few things came together all at once,” said Seroka. “Tariffs are lower than the levels we saw earlier this year and last, giving importers more certainty on costs and allowing them to replenish inventories at a quicker rate. The American economy continues to move forward, and consumers are still buying.”
September marked the 10th time Los Angeles has handled more than 500,000 loaded import containers in a month. Seroka said no other U.S. port has reached that mark once.
Despite the year-over-year increase in exports, Seroka said outbound cargo remained softer than usual. The record number of empty containers was expected, he added, as ocean carriers moved equipment back to Asia following the surge in imports.
Disruptions bring additional cargo to Los Angeles
Continued challenges along the Suez and Panama Canal routes are also sending more shipments through Los Angeles, Seroka said. He initially estimated those disruptions could increase the port’s cargo volume by about 5%, but now expects a larger gain.
Asked by Logistics Management about the next three to six months, Seroka said another trade announcement or social media post from Washington could create renewed uncertainty. Still, he expressed confidence in the port’s outlook and pointed to continued economic growth as a reason for optimism.
“But I think, in general, we look pretty good,” he said. “The American economy is still moving forward, and if we grow even at 1.5%-to 2% GDP growth, that's meaningful on a $32 trillion American economy, and it's extremely important to those trading partners we have around the world.”
For more on the port’s September results and Seroka’s outlook, read Jeff Berman’s full story in Logistics Management.

OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
23 photos
Photo: OMODA
One of the Chery Group’s latest compact SUVs, the OMODA 4, just made its European motor show debut in Paris this week, ahead of its UK market launch in 2027. This also marks OMODA&JAECOO’s first-ever appearance at the French event.
The OMODA 4 was originally unveiled at Auto China 2026, showcasing not only its futuristic styling, but also the carmaker’s proprietary Super Hybrid System (SHS-H). It’s the styling I want to focus on, though, because it’s meant to be the boldest expression yet of the brand’s so-called “Cyber Mecha” design language.
As you can see, there are a lot of sharp lines. You certainly can’t accuse the design of being old-fashioned. To me, this crossover also looks a little bit like a discount Lamborghini Urus, which both is and isn’t a bad thing.
The carmaker seems to be particularly pleased with the interior, calling it a “technology-led starship cockpit”. It was inspired by gaming and digital environments, while reflecting OMODA’s “BE THE ONE” philosophy. Like the OMODA 5, the 4 is also aimed at a younger, technology-focused buyer, which is why the cabin has somewhat of a sporty design.
To all that I say, give me a break! I mean, even the starter button looks like it’s from an Urus , featuring a red button cover. How hard is it to come up with something original? Or at least something generic. If the car is good enough on its own, it shouldn’t need to blatantly steal various design elements from other models.
Photo: Omoda Here’s what Gary Lan, CEO of OMODA&JAECOO UK had to say: “Our Paris debut is an important moment for OMODA, and it’s fantastic that OMODA 4 has now made its European motor show debut.”
“OMODA has always had a strong sense of individuality, and I think this new model really captures that while also representing an important part of the brand’s future. It’s youthful, fashion-conscious and technology-led, bringing a fresh perspective to the crossover market and appealing to customers who want something a little different.”
In terms of performance, we can expect the OMODA 4 SHS-H to feature the same drivetrain as the OMODA 5 SHS-H, meaning a hybrid system with 224 horsepower and 295 Nm (217 lb-ft) of torque. This allows the 5 to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 7.9 seconds, so the smaller 4 could be a tiny bit quicker off the mark.
There are currently three models available to UK buyers from OMODA, with the 4 set to join the group come next year. Right now, though, you can only order the OMODA 5, OMODA 7 and the 9. The entry-level 5 is priced from £24,040 in gasoline spec, but you can also get an all-electric E5 for upwards of £33,065. Meanwhile, the flagship OMODA 9 SHS-P is a $44,995 affair.

1970 Hemi Cuda With 4.10 Rear Is Full of Questions, Comes With $250K Auction Price Set in 2015
19 photos
Photo: Mecum
There are certain automobiles that will silence a room, no matter what, when, where, they are, or who’s in the room. Take the 1970 Plymouth Hemi ‘Cuda – “King of the Muscle Cars” (although, technically, it isn’t one. Muscle car, I mean) – draped in the reddest orange hue ever devised by mother Mopar, sporting the famous 426 cubic inches of hemispherical Mopar pride. Can you think of a better way to shed a quarter-million bucks of wallet bulk?
The car community is generally extremely scrupulous when it comes to certain makes and models, and the Hemicuda is certainly one of those. Gearheads put great value on documentation, provenance, originality, records, maintenance, correctness, and so on and so forth. Precisely the attributes that mostly lack from the example featured in the gallery.
It’s a 1970 E-body Plymouth with a 425-hp, 490-lb-ft big-block, alright, but nowhere does it say anything about that motor being original. Or anything about it, in general. The Mecum listing is surprisingly laconic (none of the auction house’s liability, since the consignor/seller/owner have the last say regarding what’s what about the ad), and none of the usual clues indicating great news is there.
Usually, when something’s not tier 1 quality, sellers retort to tricks like “426/425 HP V-8 hemi engine.” That takes a bit of reading between the lines. Of course, it’s a 426 Hemi, but the lack or any other detail about it typically signifies a NOM (Not Original Motor) example. That’s nothing intrinsically bad about any car, but it does hurt its value somewhat (compared to a vehicle that sports the factory-installed powerplant).
Photo: Mecum So, the Elephant is not matching the VIN. It could be a warranty replacement, or just a later addition – the question levitates freely. A warranty exchange Hemi V8 is also held in higher regard than the classic situation where the car had a transplant at some uncertain point in the past. And full disclosure is paramount – if the history of the car is known.
Speaking of history, what we do know/are told is that the paint is not original. The color is, though, which begs the question about how much of the original sheet metal is still on this pony car? The listing says “most,” which isn’t saying much. 51% is “most,” and I’d like to know what happened to the missing pieces, the ones that got replaced. Rust or bust, no two ways about it.
Either this car has been salvaged from the misfortunes of improper maintenance and whatever was corroded had to be cut off and new metal welded instead, or it has had a very physical trauma resulting from an impact with some random object. There’s no other situation that dictates employing shears and welders.
Photo: Mecum The other disclosed detail about it it’s the 4.10 Super Performance Axle package. That’s a rarity, even among the already rarefied environment of the Hemicuda realm. In 1970 – the moniker’s junior year – Plymouth built 666 examples (I like that number more than it’s socially acceptable). It was the best-selling Hemi Mopar of that year, a title that it would retain for the second and final iteration of the Mopar Hemi ponies, in 1971. After that, the 426 Hemi flapped its oversized heads into history.
Of those 666, the overwhelming majority of 652 had a proper roof over the cabin – like the one in the photos. 368 of them came with a self-shifting Torqueflite automatic transmission, with three forward speeds. The production breakdown doesn’t go beyond that limit, so there’s no carved-in-stone number for how many had the brutal 4.10 rear axle gearing.
However, Galen Govier’s registry accounts for 67 examples documented by him that have the same differential. That’s how many are known to exist today, not how many rolled off the Hamtramck assembly line in Michigan 56 years ago. That’s a little more than one in ten, but the number refers to both manuals and automatics. If evenly spread distribution comes in handy, then this Tor Red mystery machine would be one in about 35. Holy grail.
Photo: Mecum But: 1970 Hemi ‘Cuda cars came with two fender tags – in certain cases even three, depending on how long the options list was. One of those tags was reserved for the sweet “HEMI FENDER” designator. There isn’t a close-up snapshot of the fender tag(s) on this car, but there is one of the engine bay, and the solitary tag on the left front inner fender is just barely visible. The other one is not there. Maybe it was removed? Maybe it was too corroded to be restored? Maybe it was lot?
The good news is the interior is original, and there’s a pair of discs on the front brakes. The rest is visible in the photos: factory tach and rally instruments cluster, center console with a Slap Stick shifter, hemi callouts on the rear black stripes, and a shaker hood (“functional” is its described main attribute).
Almost a dozen years ago, at a Russo and Steele auction Scottsdale, Arizona, in January 2015, this car went under the gavel and came out with a $225k ear tag. The buyer paid $247,500 (10% tax for being rich enough to buy a Hemicuda), so I can only ask for your opinion on to what would this car bring on November 14, at the Mecum Las Vegas event?
Via // Mecum

2026 Mazda MX-5 Roadster and RF Get Updated Inside and Outside; This Is How Much They Cost Now
7 photos
Photo: Mazda
The Japanese automaker's local division in the Land Down Under wants to make Mazda MX-5's rivals green with envy when they see the latest updates for MY2026. But is the joke on them, since most other competitors have already switched to the 2027 model year?
Mazda is a small automaker, despite its continued large visibility triggered by iconic models like the MX-5 Miata roadster and the recent string of crossover SUV hits, which include the CX-50 produced in America as well as the regional CX-60, CX-70, CX-80, and CX-90 models. They’re even becoming known for their all-electric prowess, thanks to the Chinese-born Mazda 6e and CX-6e, recently.
Over in Australia, though, the commotion isn’t common, pun intended: Mazda is bringing few and far-off novelties to the market, like the all-new Mazda CX-6e EV crossover SUV in July, the all-new CX-5 compact crossover SUV in March, or the Mazda M Day event in October 2026. Before the sale festival begins on October 17, 2026, though, Mazda has decided to go green with the 2026 MX-5 and update it thoroughly.
The Japanese automaker speaks of a “series of thoughtful enhancements inside and out for 2026, further elevating the experience on offer in the world’s best-selling two-seat sports car.” The iconic Mazda MX-5 Miata Roadster and RF get the newly introduced Zinc Green Metallic premium color, which has been introduced also in North America and on the Old Continent as part of the latest string of updates.
It debuts in Australia on the 2026 MX-5 Roadster and RF, taking “inspiration from the color and texture of zinc chromate primer – an undercoat used to enhance the durability of industrial products – and translates rational beauty into a sense of toughness expressed through color and texture.” The other hues remain unchanged: Snowflake White Pearl Mica, Soul Red Crystal Metallic, Deep Crystal Blue Mica, Jet Black Mica, Machine Grey Metallic and Aero Grey Metallic.
The 2026 Mazda MX-5 range, meanwhile, gets Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB), which is “capable of detecting both pedestrians and cyclists (previously pedestrians only), providing greater confidence across a wider range of driving scenarios.” Lane-keep Assist System (LAS) is also added to the roster, while the MX-5 GT RS gets an exclusive additional perk.
The model introduces lightweight Recaro bucket seats trimmed in Nappa leather and genuine Alcantara with light grey stitching free of charge, as well as genuine Alcantara trim across the instrument panel, center console, console lid and door trim. “Green has been in high demand from our customers, and we’re excited to reintroduce it. This is the first time in 10 years that a green body colour has been available on a Mazda in Australia. It’s a fitting addition to the rest of the compelling updates for our globally revered sports car,” says Jarrod Gieschen, Mazda Australia Sales and Marketing Director.
The 2026 Mazda MX-5 price list kicks off with the G20 Roadster Manual version, starting at an MLP (Manufacturer’s List Price) of AU$44,590, which is the equivalent of approximately $31k at the current exchange rate. The G20 Roadster GT is available with a manual or automatic transmission for AU$51,240 or AU$52,740, while the G20 Roadster GT RS starts from AU$57,240. The prices for the RF vary between AU$55,740 and AU$61,740, meanwhile.

XPENG Reveals G9L at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Dubbed As the Ultimate "Large SUV for the AI Era"
34 photos
Photo: XPeng
Guangzhou Xiaopeng Motors Technology, commonly known as XPENG , was established less than a decade and a half ago, but it's already a major player at the 2026 Paris Motor Show in France.
XPENG (also noted as Xpeng) was born in 2014 in Guangzhou, China, but already has offices in Mountain View, California, and Munich, Germany, and trades publicly on both the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company sees itself as the purveyor of a Physical AI ecosystem spanning technology stacks, humanoid robots , flying cars, and AI-defined vehicles, including the L03, P7+, G6, G9, and X9.
The company is currently making a major appearance at the 2026 Paris Motor Show from October 12 through 18 at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, “bringing its latest advances in intelligent mobility, robotics and future transportation to one of Europe’s most prominent automotive stages.” Most importantly, the company has announced the global launch of its next-gen AI flagship SUV, the XPENG G9L, “marking another milestone in the company’s expansion in Europe.”
The stand at the Mondial de l’Auto has the theme of an immersive “Physical AI Museum” spanning four areas: the brand’s technology stack, AI-defined vehicles, humanoid robots, and flying cars. Of course, the new G9L took center stage, and XPENG has already announced that it will introduce the new flagship SUV to other regions, too, like Australia and New Zealand, without also providing the launch timing, pricing, or specifications.
Over on the Old Continent, the XPENG G9L has the XPENG NGP - Next Generation Pilot, which is the company’s next-generation intelligent driving technology, powered by a second-generation VLA model and a high-computing-power AI architecture. The VLA 2.0 will provide both city and highway assisted driving, navigation-based assisted driving, and more. XPENG intends to roll out the NGP in 2027, and the G9L also introduces XPENG’s Kunpeng Super Electric REEV technology: it combines a large battery, fast charging, efficient EV drive, and intelligent energy management.
More precisely, the XPENG G9L will have up to 287 km (WLTP) or 178 miles of EV range thanks to the REEV version featuring a large 63 kWh LFP battery pack, while the range extender system provides “long-distance flexibility when required” and extends the combined range to up to 1,200 km (WLTP) or 746 miles. Just like other REEVs (or EREVs), the G9L is driven by the electric motors in all conditions, and there’s a combined output of 430 kW or 577 hp and 695 Nm (513 lb-ft) of torque.
The company says the vehicle has no less than 24 energy-flow optimization strategies, but it’s still capable of hitting 62 mph or 100 kph in just 5.4 seconds, and the 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is relegated to working in the background, with XPENG targeting a difference of less than one dB between their Super Electric REEV and pure-electric operation under test conditions.
By the way, there will be a regular EV model, too, packing the same 430 kW or 577 hp and 695 Nm (513 lb-ft) of torque but sans the 1.5L turbo and with a larger 110-kWh battery pack that provides a rating of up to 553 km of WLTP range, or 344 miles. The model also has a DC fast-charging rating of up to 540 kW, so the 10-80% recharge would take less than 12 minutes at a suitable DC ultra-fast charging station.

The 2027 Bailey Unicorn Grande Lucena Is a Fancy Home on Wheels in Travel Trailer Disguise
14 photos
Photo: Bailey of Bristol
A rose by any other name would smell as sweet, as Shakespeare would say. This premium travel trailer (caravan) is no rose, but it's just as sweet under a different name from 2027, the Unicorn Grande Lucena.
Bailey, or Bailey of Bristol by their full name has been in the business of premium caravans and motorhomes for seven decades. They call themselves the "nation's favorite" and I assume they wouldnt be as bold as to say that out loud without proof (e.g. sales numbers) to back it up. The caveat here is that they are the favorite of a very select segment of the nation, since these are premium products throughout.
For 2027, Bailey is switching things up a bit, reorganizing their premium caravan lines under a single name, the Unicorn Family . Lite, Deluxe, and Grande are now part of this magical family, with the Grande series including four floorplans in total.
The Unicorn Grande Lucena we're looking at today is one of them. The name is entirely new, but the layout on which the model is based is actually the old and very popular Alicanto Grande Evora, tweaked here and there to be more appealing to new customers in the new year.
Photo: Bailey of Bristol Any Unicorn Grande is, as its name says, designed to be roomier, airier, more comfortable. The Lucena, for example, has maximum accommodation for four people, and it would undoubtedly be just as comfortable with four people onboard as it is with two. However, it's rear-bath layout betrays the intention for it as a couple's unit – and the most lavish of its kind.
Unicorn Grande Lucena debuted last month (September) in digital form, and then in physical form at the 2026 edition of Motorhome & Caravan Show at NEC Birmingham. You can see it toured in full in the official video at the bottom of the page, as units are preparing to head out to authorized dealers.
If you were to describe it as a premium option on a market where strict rules strictly limit available footprint, you wouldn't be wrong. The Unicorn Grande Lucena is almost as big as you can go in Europe for a travel trailer, which means that it puts other caravans to shame in terms of space, comfort, and features.
Photo: Bailey of Bristol Built on a widebody AL-KO chassis, it comes in at 7.9 meters (26 feet) of length, with an interior length of 6.57 meters (21.5 feet). It rides on a tandem axle and comes standard with AL-KO ATC and anti-sway stabilizer, AL-KO wheel lock receivers, and heavy-duty supports on all four corners.
The 2027 exterior graphics includes bronze decals that stylistically match the diamond alloy wheels and go with the Bailey distinctive curved windshield framed by large windows on either side. This allows Bailey to create inside the Unicorn Grande Lucena a lounge with outstanding panoramic views and ample natural light.
The interior is divided into three zones. You have the daytime communal areas in the front, the bedroom, and the rear bathroom that runs the entire full width of the trailer. The lounge can convert into an oversize double bed in a north-to-south disposition by simply pulling out a slatted extension from the cabinet under the windshield, but it can also be used as a bedroom with twin beds.
Photo: Bailey of Bristol By day, the same lounge is an entertaining space, whether playing games, chatting, or having a meal. Six grown adults can comfortably fit in here, and Bailey offers a pull-out snack table by the door and a standalone table for mealtimes. A TV mount (but not the TV itself), a Sonos speaker, USB and USB-C outlets, and a wireless charger are included standard .
From the lounge, you move into the kitchen space, which is generously sized thanks to the widebody chassis underneath. The L-shaped counter comes with a hybrid cooktop (three burners on gas and one hotplate), a separate grill, a separate small oven, and a compact microwave, as well as a nice sink with a rubberized flexible faucet, plenty of storage, and sufficient worktop space for meal prepping.
A large fridge with a freezer and additional storage are available across the way.
Photo: Bailey of Bristol The bedroom fits a king island bed on a tilting rail system, comparable to what they call a Versa-tilt bed in the U.S., in an east-to-west disposition, so you have ample walking space to the bathroom during the day. Bailey packs this space with the most storage options, from a little vanity slash makeup station in one corner to a full wardrobe in the other, overhead cabinets, nightstands, and a large compartment under the bed. This one is also accessible from the outside.
In the bathroom, you get a full separate shower , a cassette toilet with a heated towel rack, and a compact sink on a vanity with integrated storage. While the washroom is on the slimmer side, it still has plenty of room for movement.
The Unicorn Grande Lucena comes standard with a 130W flexible solar panel on the roof, a 40-liter (10.5-gallon) freshwater tank, a Dutch-entry door that will be appreciated by pet owners, and Alde wet central heating system in charge of the heat and the hot water.
Photo: Bailey of Bristol Maximum permissible weight for this model is 1,835 kg (4,045 lbs), of which 160 kg (353 lbs) will be payload capacity. Bailey mentions a recommended starting price for a 2027 unit of £41,999, which is approximately €49,700 or $55,600 at the current exchange rate. This figure is for reference only, since these caravans only sell within the UK.

Chris Brown’s New Four-Wheeled Toy Is a Cool Carlex Design G-Wagen
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke
Carlex Design keeps working its magic by releasing all kinds of cool custom takes on the iconic Mercedes G-Wagen, and some of these rides end up in the hands of the rich and famous.
Case in point, meet the latest project from the famous Polish tuner, which is called the Carlex Moss Vintage. This build is said to have been “inspired by nature” and “made for journey,” and and it has ended up in the possession of Chris Brown. According to Creative Bespoke, the 37-year-old American singer, songwriter, and actor, who has been active in the industry since 2002, is the proud owner of this modded Mercedes-AMG G 63, and he apparently calls it the Green Lantern.
So, what makes this particular ride that special, you ask? Well, pretty much everything when it comes to the exterior and interior, because it has been almost fully customized. But why “almost?” Because Carlex Design still does not offer power boosts for its builds, and that’s a pity, as they should definitely expand their reach to include the oily bits. But even if it does not offer more oomph, the Mercedes-AMG G 63 is still very potent, and that’s without any mods whatsoever.
But what does that mean exactly? Well, since we’ve started talking about the powertrain, we might as well remind you that 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) is a 4.3-second affair in the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63. The model has 577 horsepower (585 ps/430 kW) available via the right pedal and 627 pound-feet (850 Nm) of torque. That is how much the V8 engine, with its bi-turbo and 4.0-liter displacement, churns out.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke Sporting a bi-tone look that mixes green on the lower parts of the body with black on the pillars and roof, this particular Mercedes-AMG G 63 also benefits from a few other enhancements. For instance, it has a new bumper at the front that looks like it came from a long-gone era. The Panamericana grille, which has vertical slats on the standard G 63, has been replaced by a new one with horizontal slats, which is decorated with the Carlex Design logo in the middle.
The three-pointed star emblem proudly sits on the hood, and this vehicle appears to feature power running boards for enhanced ingress and egress. The rear bumper is also new, and shaped to look like a classic one, and from what we can tell, the wheel arches are a bit more pronounced. A pinstripe-like element also decorates this Mercedes-AMG G 63, and the ride also sports some chrome accents here and there for a more vintage look.
Speaking of “vintage,” this word is best used to describe the wheels. If you are familiar with Carlex Design’s work, then you know that they have recently introduced quite a few Mercedes-AMG G 63 SUVs that feature these exact wheels. These combine silver and green, and they were shod in new tires with a partial white wall look. Last but not least, when it comes to the exterior, anyway, is the custom spare wheel holder attached to the rear door. Well, this and the usual Carlex Design emblems.
Opening the door will reveal a very classy-looking interior. Here, the Polish tuner signed the entire upholstery. This includes the chequered design on the seats and on the right side of the dashboard panel, as well as the leather upholstery wrapped around the seats outer edges, the upper and lower parts of the dashboard panel, the center console, steering wheel, door cards, and other parts of the cockpit.
Photo: Instagram | creativebespoke The seatbacks and headrests are home to some special logos, the pillars and headliner have been wrapped in Alcantara, and there is also new trim on deck, as far as we can tell. And in plain Carlex Design fashion, we would not be surprised at all to learn that the fully custom interior has a better overall quality than the stock one.
And to be honest, this particular Mercedes-AMG G 63 is definitely an automotive work of art capable of turning heads wherever it goes. Thus, congratulations to the peeps at Carlex Design for pulling yet another cool project, and one that has a very famous owner, because the so-called Green Lantern is definitely something to write home about.
We would have loved to wrap things up by revealing how much Chris Brown paid for the Carlex Design Moss Vintage, but the truth is that we do not know. Nevertheless, this build is definitely no bargain, and if we were to guess, we’d say that it has likely been well over half a million dollars. However, you may want to refrain from quoting us on that number, as that’s our two cents, and should be taken accordingly.
A brand new Mercedes- AMG G 63, on the other hand, will set you back a minimum of $198,750 in the United States of America for the latest model year, and that’s before destination, options, and dealer fees. Jeep Concludes the Bold Twelve 4 Twelve Series With a Grand Finale: 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback
7 photos
Photo: Jeep
Stellantis knows that Jeep needs to get back in the saddle after the sales fall, and they spared no expense, including for the iconic Wrangler nameplate. But you don’t need to take our word for granted, because the Twelve 4 Twelve series is a great example.
It’s been a minute since Jeep was casually strolling through the US and international charts as the most popular brand that Stellantis has to offer. Now it has to work hard again to earn back its place, as Jeep only holds a narrow lead year-to-date in America in 2026, while Ram became the best-selling brand across the US automotive market during the third quarter of the year.
With almost 414k units delivered across nine months, Jeep remains ahead of Ram with 369k vehicles, but it actually dropped eight percent while the truck brand jumped 20% in the charts, and Ram sold 134k units during Q3 of 2026 whereas Jeep had a little over 128k sales, compounding a 29% jump against a steep 20% drop. Anyway, Jeep is doing what it can to keep the interest high for the iconic Wrangler line.
While everyone was paying attention to the 2026 Paris Motor Show in France, where Jeep itself outlined its roadmap to 2030 on the Old Continent, at home in America the Stellantis brand revealed the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback, the 12th and final release in its Twelve 4 Twelve series – the “culmination of a yearlong celebration of Wrangler’s heritage, capability, design and enduring connection with generations of enthusiasts.”
The series took inspiration from Wrangler’s military roots and iconic eras to western culture, retro design, concept vehicles and even the owners “who have made Wrangler their own.” For the bold grand finale, the focus is turning toward the horizon, with the Switchback inspired by the “bold colors, graphic treatments and mix-and-match creativity of contemporary gaming and digital culture.”
So, it mixes things up: Black and Sting-Gray dual vented power dome hoods and doors can be switched across complementary configurations, “creating the impression of sibling Wranglers swapping parts,” while the Gecko hue is now a high-impact accent on the grille surround, hood graphic and beadlock wheel rings, and there’s even a special Gecko finish developed for the wheel ring.
The swapping idea is also implemented in production: Gloss Black and Sting-Gray vehicles are built together across the line, then doors get switched during the regular production process, and hoods get swapped at the upfitting center to achieve the contrasting look of the Wrangler Switchback.
Exterior details include Gecko accents, Gloss Black or Sting-Gray power dome hood and doors, Sting-Gray or Gloss Black “Switchback” hood graphic and Sting-Gray “41” body-side decals, Gloss Black or Sting-Gray three-piece hardtops, Black Jeep and Trail Rated badges, and Black tow hooks to complete the package.
Inside, the new Switchback has the same contrasting theme with Global Black and Sea Salt Nappa leather, Lime accent stitching, linear graphic treatments, a bespoke Switchback cupholder plaque and swing-gate plaque add exclusive graphic details, plus a Willys satin chrome shifter medallion and unique HVAC vent graphics “featuring the iconic seven-slot grille and Willys silhouette, subtle nods to Jeep brand heritage and Willys roots.”
Ordering for the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback will open in November 2026, and the package is priced at $2,870. It’s based on the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Rubicon X, so the MSRP is $66,695 for the two-door model and $69,995 for the four-door model, including the $1,995 destination charge.

Sikorsky Designs Containerized Fast Pack Launch Kit for One of the Wackiest Drones Around
11 photos
Photo: Sikorsky
With the exception of the Cypher design of the late 1980s, helicopter maker Sikorsky didn’t really step into the world of uncrewed aerial systems (UAS). That changed recently, when the company entered the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s (DARPA) AdvaNced airCraft Infrastructure-Less Launch And RecoverY (ANCILLARY) program back in 2023.
The effort is meant to come up with vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) drones that can be operated without specialized tools and can fly from the most austere of environments. As per the requirements of the program, the hybrid-electric-powered designs have to weigh 300 pounds (136 kg) and be able to carry a 60-pound (27 kg) payload.
Sikorsky’s answer to DARPA’s request was something called the Nomad 50, presented in the spring of 2024. Seeing the impact it could have on military operations, but not only that, the company turned the design into a family of drones. And it’s the larger Nomad 100 that’s the focus of our story today.
The design performed its first flight in the summer of this year, so it’s not really operational yet. That isn’t stopping the helicopter maker from imagining new ways of deploying and operating the drone in the hands of the military.
Remember Ukraine’s Operation Spiderweb from the summer of 2025 against five Russian Air Force bases deep inside Russia, which involved the use of drones hidden inside civilian trucks? That’s the first thing that came to mind when stumbling upon Sikorsky’s Nomad 100 fast pack idea.
Photo: Sikorsky What we’re dealing with is basically a containerized launch kit for the Nomad 100 , centered around a single 20‑foot (six meters) ISO container that can hold a total of four such drones, but also the required mission‑command software, power, communications, and sustainment equipment.
The idea behind this concept is that, instead of transporting individual drones or launching them from afar, operators can deploy the container in austere and infrastructure-limited locations, from where they can launch the Nomads on the heads of unsuspecting enemies.
The American defense contractor says this setup allows maximum mobility, rapid set‑up, and minimal personnel requirements, promising that two of the Nomads housed inside the container can be ready to fly on missions in as little as 15 minutes, while the other two over the next four to six hours. Not exactly as fast as what we’ve seen during Operation Spiderweb, then again, we’re talking about entirely different kinds of drones.
Sikorsky’s kit has been designed to be used from remote areas, but also naval vessels and staging areas. Because it’s a container we’re talking about, it can rapidly be moved to where it’s needed, ready to fulfill missions ranging from reconnaissance and light attack to contested logistics and more benign uses such as forestry and firefighting.
Photo: Sikorsky For now, this idea is more like a concept, as the Nomad 100 drone it’s meant to serve is not really ready for duty. It only recently performed its first flight, completing the initial ground and flight testing. That also means its technical specifications are kept under wraps for now.
We do know, though, that as far as drones are concerned, this one is pretty wacky. That’s because we’re dealing with a rotor-blown wing design.
What this means is that we’re basically talking about a tail-sitting aircraft shaped like a flying wing. It has motors and propellers installed toward its tips, and vertical structures to the left and right that act like landing legs.
This design allows the drone to take off and land like any other helicopter in the world, then, as soon as a certain altitude is reached, switches to a mode of operation akin to that of a fixed-wing aircraft.
What makes this a proprotor is the fact that it uses the same propellers to climb and fly, making air move over the proprotor wash and across the wing. This means there’s less drag when hovering and when transitioning to horizontal flight.
Photo: Sikorsky Sikorsky never said what powers the drone, but, as per the requirements of the DARPA program, we expect to see a hybrid-electric powertrain. The company’s Matrix autonomous solution is what makes up the drone’s mind.
After announcing the drone’s first flight this summer, the company also said the Nomad family of drones will enter an intensive flight test campaign. It is supposed to unfold at an unnamed government facility, where engineers will try to replicate the many use-case scenarios for the drone. We have no information on how that’s going at the time of writing.
When ready for duty, the Nomad could also be used in loyal wingman roles in support of crewed aircraft, but we’re yet to see any steps being made to prove this capability.
The Sikorsky UAS was not the only one developed for the DARPA program, whose status is currently unclear. The list also included the AeroVironment Wildcat and drones made by Griffon Aerospace, Karem Aircraft, and Method Aeronautics.

2026 Paris Motor Show: Jeep Reveals Six-Model European Strategy for 2030, Renegade Is Set to Return
10 photos
Photo: Jeeep
Stellantis had a massive presence at the 2026 edition of the Mondial de l'Auto at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles in France, and Jeep wasn't neglected even though it actually didn’t come with any new models on the catwalk.
The French-Italian-American automaker Stellantis has just reported its estimated consolidated sales for the third quarter of the year, and with 1.3 million global deliveries it almost stopped the bleeding – they’re down just one percent year-over-year. At home in Europe, they’re up ten percentage points thanks to all-electric models, but in North America they still have their work cut out for them, as the region is down 12%.
Anyway, Stellantis decided to make the Old Continent its prime star for the month of October, and that meant one major event – the 2026 Paris Motor Show , where it arrived with more than 60 vehicles across its stands, nine of them being concept cars. They even held an exclusive preview event, ‘The Night Before’ the Mondial de l’Auto, where they presented no less than six of their nine planned concept cars for the event – just like during the good old days before the pandemics.
The stars of the event were Alfa Romeo, Citroen, DS Automobiles, Fiat, Opel, and Peugeot, but now it’s time to talk about one beloved American brand that was also present at the 2026 Paris Motor Show even though it didn’t have a new model or a concept car to showcase in a dedicated world premiere: Jeep.
At home in America, they just completed the spectacular Twelve for Twelve special edition series for the Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator with the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback inspired by both the brand’s legacy as well as the contemporary world of gaming, but over in Europe the accent is on the upcoming business strategy at the moment.
More precisely, Jeep has outlined its European roadmap for 2030 at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, and the ‘Road to 2030’ vision outlined by Xavier Peugeot, Head of Jeep Brand Enlarged Europe: "Jeep will rely on its strong values, capitalize on the successful launches of the new Avenger and new Compass, and reinforce its position in Europe by expanding its range up to six models, multi-energy and multi-platform, by 2030," explained the manager.
The next steps for the brand are now clear: the next generation Jeep Renegade will return by 2030, “reclaiming a key position in the brand’s expanding portfolio by 2030”; the European range will be expanded to six models by 2030, and the company is also mulling a potential return to the large D-segment. Then, beyond 2030, “Jeep is exploring how its iconic DNA can shape new mobility solutions for a rapidly changing world.”
Back to the Jeep Renegade, a subcompact crossover SUV produced from 2015 through 2025 in Europe , since its launch, more than 610k units have been sold on the Old Continent, “making it a key contributor to Jeep’s success in the region.” So, a new generation will potentially stimulate the brand’s position on the continent and also attract additional buyers for the company.
Jeep also wants to strengthen its presence in the subcompact, compact, and mid-size SUV segments in Europe: the Avenger has already sold almost 300k units since its arrival in 2023, and the new Compass generation is directly aimed at the ultra-competitive compact CUV segment. Above them, the Jeep Recon will mark the brand’s return to the D-SUV segment, while an additional all-new model will arrive in 2028.

All-New Axiom Grit 3814 Fifth Wheel Toy Hauler Delivers a Premium Experience at a Smaller Price
40 photos
Photo: Axiom RV
Exactly one year ago, a new name exploded on the RV market with a pair of products that defied all expectations regarding fifth wheelers: Axiom RV. One year after this stellar debut, Axiom is hard at work to build on it, adding to those initial two series more budget-friendly variants.
Axiom's debut included the Vendetta fifth wheel toy hauler and the Imperium luxury fifth wheel RV, each with a couple of more floorplans to choose from and several options you could add to get an even nicer experience. For 2027, each of these series is getting a price-conscious alternative: Imperium with the Avora and Vendetta with the Grit.
Both Avora and Grit will be standalone series with four floorplans in between them, two for each, and both made their debut last month (September) at a U.S. trade event. Today's focus is Grit, the Grit 3814 specifically, which is a family-friendly toy hauler with all the features Axiom has come to be famous for but a lower price tag than the Vendetta it's inspired by.
Since this is still a pre-production floorplan, it's not even featured on the official Axiom page yet among the available products. But Grit 3814 does get a landing page, official photos, and minimum specs, as well as a nice introductory walkthrough video you will find at the bottom of the page. In short, we have all we need to get a nice appreciation of an upcoming product in all its (oversize) glory.
Photo: Axiom RV First off, Axiom is keen to underline that, despite the price-conscious angle to the Grit toy hauler, it's still an Axiom product getting the Axiom staple features that drew international attention last year. That means all-steel construction, extra tall ceilings, extra tall slide-outs with flush floor, residential finishes and appliances, residential mini-split system for HVAC, and a generator moved behind the axle, under the chassis, for the largest pass-through storage compartment of the entire class.
This might be a more "budget" product, but make no mistake about it, it's still top of its class, still premium in every way that counts. It's like the Vendetta before it but with some costs shaved off here and there.
The Grit 3814 is the first of the planned line, a triple-axle three-slide widebody toy hauler that's equally suitable for hauling toys as it's to accommodate the entire family. It's different from its more higher-end predecessors by its gray and white paintjob, which it shares with the Avora. Suspension is a downgraded Curt leaf spring suspension instead of TCS independent suspension, with Solera legged awnings instead of Gerard armless ones.
Photo: Axiom RV The Pathfinder lighting system is still present, as you'd expect, since it sets Axiom RVs apart from all the other big boys and girls out there. This unit comes in at 43 feet 10 inches (13.3 meters) in length, 14 feet (4.2 meters) of which are dedicated to the garage space, and 13 feet 5 inches (4 meters) of height.
The Grit 3814 is a front bedroom floorplan with Axiom-standard picture windows, all of them Euro square, frameless ones, premium custom cabinetry with soft-close hinges, dovetail joinery, and adjustable shelves, and residential appliances.
The main entrance is in one of the campsite slide-outs, directly into the open-plan kitchen and living space. This allows Axiom to put an expandable standalone dinette by the door, with a full fridge and pantry on the other side. This also allows Axiom to offer full access to the fridge with the slide closed, which apparently was a very requested customer demand.
Photo: Axiom RV In front of the entrance is the living room , with a gorgeous L-shaped sectional with integrated recliners and an entertainment center with a 55-inch smart TV, an electric fireplace, and a JBL portable speaker. Storage is integrated throughout, wherever possible, which is great considering this is meant as a family-friendly solution even for extended stays.
The kitchen is a horseshoe-shaped unit with the kitchen peninsula sliding in and out of the main kitchen block with the corresponding slide-out. It might seem a compact kitchen but it's very nicely appointed, from the all-accessory sink to the four-burner cooktop and the large microwave, and storage and prep space galore.
Another customer demand integrated into this Grit floorplan is the addition of an entrance to the garage loft from the kitchen space. Basically, you can use the same ladder you use in the garage to get to the loft, but from the kitchen side.
Photo: Axiom RV Speaking of the garage, it's the highlight of the floorplan . It's designed for toys, even larger side-by-sides, but it can also double as a secondary bedroom with its separate bathroom facilities and entertainment. A split collapsible bathroom, a mini-split, a TV, and a combination of a HappiJac sofa and drop-down double bed are all included in the standard package.
At the front of the trailer is the bathroom and main bedroom, in typical fifth wheel fashion. In the bathroom, you'll find a one-piece fiberglass shower with a rain head, a porcelain toilet, and a small sink on a slimline vanity that integrates some storage.
The bedroom comes with a king bed in a slide-out, a dresser, and a full wardrobe in the front cap. Axiom erases the large windshield in that front cap to offer more storage, also based on customer requests, and the result is a wardrobe with hanging space and a separate closet with washer-dryer prep.
Photo: Axiom RV The Grit 3814 comes standard with Victron energy power system and 400W of solar on the roof, upgradable to as much as 3200W through the AX Boondocker series packages, six-point hydraulic leveling, Fogatti on-demand water heater, and Starlink prep. Dry weight is 16,500 lbs (7,484 kg), with a reported gross weight of 24,000 lbs (10,886 kg).
Axiom says this fifth wheel toy hauler is designed for "travelers who demand maximum space in a manageable footprint without compromising," and that will mean a price tag worthy of the "uncompromising" descriptor. MSRP will be at around $193,000 before options. It's cost-conscious only in relation to the Axiom Vendetta, which is about $50K more expensive in base configuration.
